verdict.rationale: Angular's docs highlight fine-grained reactivity via Signals and community reports confirm AOT-compilation and strong rendering performance (angular-docs-1, angular-comm-2, angular-comm-19), supporting the idea of compiler-driven efficient updates rather than manual diffing. However, there's no explicit documentation of the Ivy compiler's template-to-instruction translation mechanism or its surgical DOM-update strategy, and older community threads reference a dirty-checking digest cycle with scalability limits (angular-comm-6, angular-comm-10) that is at odds with 'surgical' updates, though those refer to legacy AngularJS behavior. missing for 10: explicit first-party docs describing the Ivy compiler's template compilation to fine-grained DOM instructions, independent benchmarks isolating compiler-driven update efficiency vs manual diffing.
